mcp_tool_registry.note: There is no separate 'Tool Registry' module. The registry IS the `TOOLS` dict (lines 364-378) + `_tool_defs()` (546-555) + `_handle()` dispatcher (558-593) in this one 411-line file. Any TDR referencing 'Tool Registry' should point here, not go looking for a distinct component.
current_protocol_state: PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2025-06-18" (line 43); SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS also lists 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 (line 45) — none of these is the OWNER-REPORT's cited 2026-07-28 revision.

`initialize` is still a live, functioning method in `_handle()` (lines 561-569), returning protocolVersion/capabilities/serverInfo — this is exactly the handshake the OWNER-REPORT says the 2026-07-28 revision removes. It has NOT been removed here.

A stateless HTTP transport variant DOES already exist: `_StatelessHTTPHandler` (lines 399-514), explicitly stateless per spec 2025-06-18's 'Streamable HTTP' mode — rejects any `Mcp-Session-Id` header with 400 'stateless-server-no-sessions' (line 490-492), attributed in the docstring to 'مگاپرامپتِ G5' (line 16).
No `Mcp-Method` / `Mcp-Name` headers exist anywhere in this file — those are specific to the OWNER-REPORT's cited 2026-07-28 revision and are not implemented.

CONCLUSION: this server already implements an adjacent-but-different statelessness (the optional 2025-06-18 stateless HTTP transport, i.e. no session ID) — it does NOT yet implement the OWNER-REPORT's cited 2026-07-28 full-protocol revision (which additionally drops the initialize handshake entirely in favor of per-request Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name headers). These should not be conflated as 'already done'.

policy_gate.note: This is almost certainly what the owner-report means by 'PolicyGate'. Read lines 1-90 (ADR-033, fail-closed authorization gate).
policy_gate.finding: PolicyGate is already a pure function over an explicit, frozen `RequestContext` dataclass (run_id, checkpoint_id, state_version, policy_version, actor, action, trust_level, provenance_id, approval_id, idempotency_key, kill_switch_engaged — all passed in per call, lines 22-33). It holds no session state of its own and was never coupled to MCP's initialize/Mcp-Session-Id handshake — those are two unrelated layers (MCP is the transport bringing a request in; PolicyGate is a separate ADR-033 decision function invoked with an explicit context, regardless of transport). CORRECTION to owner-report framing: the claim that MCP going stateless 'directly affects PolicyGate' does not hold up against the actual code — there is no session dependency in policy_gate.py to remove. The real MCP-layer work is scoped to server.py's initialize handling and headers, not to PolicyGate.
